name: IRS21864STRPBF
title: IRS2186(4)(S)PBF 600 V high and low side gate driver, 4 A / 4 A
summary: A high-voltage gate driver for power MOSFETs and IGBTs with separate outputs for the high side and the low side switch, each set by its own in-phase logic input. The high side floats on a bootstrap supply and works up to +600 V offset; both channels have undervoltage lockout and drive 4 A source and sink. The IRS2186 (8-lead) ties logic and power ground together at COM; the IRS21864 (14-lead) has a separate logic ground VSS that may sit ±5 V from COM. Inputs accept 3.3 V and 5 V logic.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IRS2186(S)
circuits.description: Drives a pair of N-channel MOSFETs on a rail of up to 600 V from two logic inputs, HIN for the high side and LIN for the low side. VCC powers the chip and charges the bootstrap capacitor C2 through D1; C2, between VB and VS, is the high side driver's supply. C1 bypasses VCC to COM. HO and LO reach the gates through R1 and R2. COM, the low side source and the rail capacitor C3 share ground. The high side source (VS) and the low side drain are brought out to two load terminals.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IRS21864(S)
circuits.description: The same half bridge as the 8-lead part, with a separate logic ground. The input side refers to VSS, which comes out as its own terminal, and C1 bypasses VCC to VSS; C4 bypasses VCC to COM, the power ground shared with the low side source and the rail capacitor C3. VCC charges the bootstrap capacitor C2 through D1, and C2 feeds the high side driver between VB and VS. HO and LO drive the gates through R1 and R2; VS and the low side drain go to two load terminals.

operation.text: Two independent gate drivers: a low side channel referred to COM and a floating high side channel referred to VS, each with its own in-phase logic input. HIN high turns HO on, LIN high turns LO on.

The high side channel is built to run from a bootstrap supply between VB and VS. It operates with VS up to +600 V, tolerates negative transients on VS and is immune to dV/dt up to 50 V/ns. Its logic works for VS from -5 V to 600 V; with VS between -5 V and -VBS the output state is held.

VCC and VBS each run from 10 V to 20 V, and each has an internal 20 V clamp. Both channels have undervoltage lockout: the rising threshold is 8.9 V typical (8 V to 9.8 V), the falling threshold 8.2 V typical (7.4 V to 9 V), the hysteresis 0.7 V typical (0.3 V minimum).

HIN and LIN take standard CMOS or LSTTL levels down to 3.3 V logic: a high is 2.5 V or more and a low 0.8 V or less over VCC from 10 V to 20 V. On the IRS21864 the inputs refer to VSS, which may be up to 5 V either side of COM; on the IRS2186 VSS and COM are one pin.

Each output buffer sources and sinks 4 A typical, 2 A minimum, measured as a pulse of 10 µs or less into a shorted output. The stage is designed to keep cross-conduction inside the driver low, and its di/dt is limited for noise immunity.
Into 1000 pF at 15 V, turn-on and turn-off delays are 170 ns typical (250 ns maximum), rise time 22 ns and fall time 18 ns typical. The two channels' delays match to within 35 ns.

Propagation delays run from the input crossing 50 % to the output crossing 10 % (turn-on) or 90 % (turn-off). Rise time runs from 10 % to 90 % of the output, fall time from 90 % to 10 %. Delay matching MT is the difference between the high side and low side delays for the same edge.
The SOIC parts come in tubes or on 2500-piece reels (TR in the part number); the PDIP parts come in tubes only.
